text: The sun went down. The first pale stars came out.
Sunny sat and watched the sky grow deep and blue.
Then, soft and low from somewhere in the dark,
a gentle call: “boo-book… boo-book…” drifting near.
A little boobook owl, all brown and soft,
with great round eyes like two warm golden moons.
She sat upon a branch and blinked at Sunny,
her feathers fluffed against the cooling night.
“Hello,” said Sunny. “What a lovely call.”
“I sing the bush to sleep,” the owl replied.
She spread her wings and glided soft and slow,
silent as a shadow through the trees.
“I watch the night,” she whispered, gliding back.
“So all the little ones can safely dream.”
So Sunny watched the stars come twinkling out,
and felt how safe the gentle night could be.
The owl called softly, “boo-book,” low and warm,
a lullaby that floated on the breeze.
She settled in her hollow, snug and round,
and tucked her beak beneath a downy wing.
Sunny found a nook among the ferns,
and curled up cosy in the quiet dark.
The bush was still. The moon was soft and round.
Everything was peaceful, safe, and calm.
Her eyes grew heavy as the owl kept watch.
One slow blink… then another… then no more.
And Sunny slept beneath the watching owl,
safe and warm and dreaming through the night.
Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, gentle owl.
Goodnight, sleepy bush. Goodnight, little one.
